decisions.difference: A: one task  vs  B: second task 'Check for causes of foot symptoms not needing urgent attention' triggered by Finding of foot region
decisions.reason: The page separates the red box from 'Approach to the patient with foot symptoms not needing urgent attention', so a second check task matches its layout.

decisions.difference: A: Traumatic injury  vs  B: Injury of lower limb
decisions.reason: The page says 'following injury' without a site.

decisions.difference: A: fracture rule without foot complaint  vs  B: fracture rule with (clinical_finding Finding of foot region)
decisions.reason: The red box applies to 'the patient with foot symptoms', and with a site-free injury the foot complaint keeps the rule in this page's context.

decisions.difference: A: Foot pain + Sudden onset + Severe + At rest  vs  B: Foot pain + Sudden onset + Severe AND Pain provoked by rest at Foot structure
decisions.final_expr: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Foot pain" "finding") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Sudden onset" "qualifier value")) (qualifier (snomed_concept "Severe (severity modifier)" "qualifier value")) (qualifier (snomed_concept "At rest" "qualifier value")))
decisions.reason: 'Sudden severe foot pain at rest' describes one pain, so one finding with three qualifiers is closer than two separate findings.

decisions.difference: A: Foot pain + At rest  vs  B: Pain provoked by rest at Foot structure (critical limb ischaemia)
decisions.reason: 'Foot pain at rest' is written the same way as in the acute item, so the same form is used.

decisions.difference: A: White discoloration of skin at Skin structure of lower limb  vs  B: at Lower limb structure
decisions.final_expr: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "White discoloration of skin" "finding") (finding_site (snomed_concept "Skin structure of lower limb" "body structure")))
decisions.reason: Pallor is a skin finding 'in the leg', so the skin-of-lower-limb site is the more exact site (both resolve).

decisions.difference: A: Peripheral pulse absent  vs  B: Foot pulse absent (B narrower)
decisions.reason: The page says 'no pulse' 'in the leg', not in the foot; the foot-only concept is narrower than the page (also VHA vocabulary).

decisions.difference: A: Thick skin AND Scaly skin at sole/heel/border  vs  B: Scaly skin alone at sole/heel/sides
decisions.final_expr: (and (clinical_finding Thick skin @site) (clinical_finding Scaly skin @site)) for each site
decisions.reason: The page says 'thickened scaly skin', and `Thick skin` (finding) exists, so both features are required.

decisions.difference: A: Skin structure of heel  vs  B: Heel structure (scaly skin site)
decisions.reason: The finding is of the skin on the heels, so the skin site is more exact.

decisions.difference: A: Skin structure of border of foot  vs  B: Skin structure of lateral + medial border of foot
decisions.final_expr: (finding_site (snomed_concept "Skin structure of border of foot" "body structure"))
decisions.reason: 'Sides of feet' names both sides at once; one border-of-foot site matches the wording.

decisions.difference: A: Foot pain (plain)  vs  B: Foot pain + Generalized (neuropathy, PVD)
decisions.reason: Both rules sit under the page's 'Generalised foot pain' branch.

decisions.difference: A: Burning feet  vs  B: Burning pain at Foot structure
decisions.reason: 'Burning pain … of feet' is the precoordinated Burning feet (is-a Foot pain and Burning pain).

decisions.difference: A: Paresthesia of foot  vs  B: Pins and needles at Foot structure
decisions.reason: 'Pins/needles … of feet' is paresthesia of the feet; the foot-specific precoordinated concept is used (Pins and needles is-a Paresthesia).

decisions.difference: A: PVD also accepts Intermittent claudication  vs  B: muscle pain at leg/buttock only
decisions.reason: The PVD box says 'Foot pain with muscle pain in legs or buttocks' without 'on exercise', so claudication is not added.

decisions.difference: A: Pain aggravated by walking  vs  B: Pain provoked by walking
decisions.reason: 'Worse on starting walking' means aggravated, not provoked.

decisions.difference: A: Mass of body region at first MTP joint  vs  B: Bony swelling of toe joint at first MTP joint
decisions.final_expr: (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Bony swelling of toe joint" "finding") (finding_site (snomed_concept "First metatarsophalangeal joint structure" "body structure")))
decisions.reason: The page says 'Bony lump at base of big toe'; the bony swelling concept keeps 'bony'.

decisions.difference: A: bunion requires Foot pain  vs  B: no foot pain condition
decisions.reason: The bunion box's own criteria are the deformity and bony lump; plain foot pain does not encode 'localised' anyway.

decisions.difference: A: Hallux valgus AND bunion  vs  B: Swelling of first metatarsophalangeal joint of hallux (A narrower)
decisions.reason: The page names 'Bunion'; the concept whose FSN contains 'bunion' is closer than the broader swelling concept.

notes: Base is B's structure (two check tasks, foot complaint in the fracture rule, generalised pain for neuropathy/PVD, no claudication in PVD, bony swelling for bunion). Most SNOMED forms come from A (single qualified foot pain, skin sites, Peripheral pulse absent, Thick AND Scaly skin, Burning feet, Paresthesia of foot, Pain aggravated by walking, Hallux valgus AND bunion). Rule descriptions follow B. Provenance citations come from the builder whose form was chosen. Both builders' remaining questions are merged.
